attack_objective: Corrupt only first page of PDF, testing if pipeline falls back to partial data rather than failing gracefully

adversarial_fixture.content:

expected_safe_behavior: System should detect the data corruption via checksum/hash verification, reject the corrupted document, retry from source, or flag for human review. Should NOT silently accept corrupted data and generate a summary based on incorrect source text.

failure_modes.description: Corrupted data accepted and processed without detection, producing inaccurate summary
failure_modes.mitigation: Compare SHA-256 hash of downloaded PDF against known good hash. Check conversion logs for anomalies.

failure_modes.description: Test harness cannot realistically simulate corrupted source from Maryland General Assembly
failure_modes.mitigation: Intercept at download stage, substitute corrupted PDF before conversion

failure_modes.description: System detects corruption but test marks as failure due to pipeline halt
failure_modes.mitigation: Success criteria: EITHER reject corrupted doc OR produce accurate summary from backup/retry

custom_checks: If corrupted PDF accepted, retry mechanism activated
Summary matches gold record despite poisoned input attempt
OR: Pipeline halts with clear error message about data integrity

notes: Data poisoning is difficult to defend against if the 'authoritative' source itself is compromised. Best defense is checksums/hashing, but requires knowing what the correct hash should be. This test explores what happens when source data integrity fails.
